newsitem.title: UK: Williams profits rise, says Europe markets tough.
newsitem.headline: Williams profits rise, says Europe markets tough.

text.p: Williams Holdings, the British-based fire protection, security products and building products group, warned on Tuesday of "clear evidence" of persistently tough market conditions in continental Europe. The group posted an 11.4 percent rise in first-half pretax profits to a record 114.9 million pounds ($179.2 million) and said its second half depended on the continuing strength of its fire protection arms and higher sales of security products worldwide.
But Williams said that improved market conditions for building products in North America would continue to help offset the effects of subdued markets in Europe.

"Order books in July and August have confirmed the trends of the first half with pleasing performances in the fire and security businesses, but clear evidence of continued challenging market conditions in continental Europe," chairman Sir Nigel Rudd said in a statement.

Williams Holdings said it had developed its businesses through strict cost control, increased capital investment and a 212.5 million pounds spend on acquisitions. The company said continued strong operational cash flow combined with a 27 percent rise in capital expenditure. It raised the dividend by 5.5 percent to 5.8 pence from 5.5 pence.
The sale of its electronics businesses for 71 million pounds to management in July helped the group concentrate on core business areas, the company said.
"...the benefits of this strategy will be further evident in both the performance and strategic development of the group during the remainder of the year," Rudd said.
A small exceptional gain is expected on the disposal, which will be reflected in the second half of 1996, the company said. ($1=.6412 Pound)
